units.title: Background: What is physiology?
units.summary: • Physiology is scientific study of: • normal conditions and activities of a living organism • and functions and mechanisms of body parts for maintaining survival. • Content of “human physiology”: • (1) Normal conditions of human body • (2) Functions of human cells, tissues, and organs for achieving normal conditions • The structures and positions of human body parts are highly related to their functions! • Thus, learning (3) basic anatomy of each organ is essential for understanding the physiological functions!

units.title: Organization of Human Body and Organ-System Overview

units.title: Important Chemicals in Human Body
units.summary: Important Chemicals in Human Body • Human body is made of chemicals • Four types of important chemicals in human body • Water • Carbohydrates • Lipids • Proteins Important Chemicals in Human Body • Water • Most abundant inorganic compound (60%–80% of volume of living cells) • Important functions: • (1) Useful solvent • Dissolves many substances for chemical reactions in body • Body’s major transport medium • (2) Stabilize body temperature • Example: Sweating • (3) Cushioning to protect organs • Example: cerebrospinal fluid cushions nervous system organs • (4) Lubricant to enhance movement • Example: synovial fluid in joints Important Chemicals in Human Body • Carbohydrates • Simple sugars and complex carbohydrates • Molecules are made up of 3 types of atoms - C, H, and O • Three classes 3 • (1) Monosaccharides: simple sugars • (2) Disaccharides: combination of 2 monosaccharides • (3) Polysaccharides: complex carbohydrates Important Chemicals in Human Body • Monosaccharides • Contain 3-7 carbon atoms in each molecules • General formula: (CH 2 O) n (n: number of carbon atoms) • Common monosaccharides • Glucose (blood sugar): • Directly used by cells for energy production Important Chemicals in Human Body • Disaccharides (Double sugars) • Combination of two monosaccharides by dehydration • Too large to pass through cell membranes • Must be broken into monosaccharides before entering cells
